outcome: Rota's basis conjecture is still open in every source I could open (latest checks October 2026). Since 26 January 2024 the only results touching it are asymptotic: Montgomery and Sauermann (arXiv 2508.05601, 7 August 2025) prove (1−o(1))n disjoint transversal bases and (1+o(1))n covering transversal bases for large n, and Arndt et al. (arXiv 2604.03735, 4 April 2026) make an asymptotic variant constructive without proving any instance. A toy-scale AlphaEvolve experiment on F₂-linear matroids of rank 5 to 13 (Bérczi, arXiv 2603.06692, 4 March 2026) states that it does not resolve the conjecture. I found no resolution, no counterexample and no AI-produced proof of the conjecture.
problem_asks: Read from the statement alone. (1) For every n, the claim is quantified over all ranks n (the statement says 'matroids of rank n'). (2) For every matroid M of rank n. (3) For every family of n pairwise disjoint bases B₁,…,Bₙ of M, so n² distinct elements in all. (4) Existence of an n×n arrangement of those n² elements in which row i is exactly the set Bᵢ. (5) Every column of that arrangement is a basis of M. Equivalent form used in the literature: n pairwise disjoint transversal bases, each taking one element from each Bᵢ, with the transversals as the columns. The Wikipedia article also states the vector-space case (an n-dimensional vector space, n bases) and a plane-geometry version with three triangles of three colours; both are special cases of (1) to (5). The problem asks for existence, not for a count, and for no particular field.

events.what_happened: Huang and Rota published the statement in 1994 (Discrete Mathematics), crediting it to Rota's 1989 work without citation. They showed that the Alon–Tarsi conjecture on even versus odd Latin squares would imply the vector-space version for even n over fields of characteristic zero. This is a conditional result. Not opened: the year comes from the Open Problem Garden reference list and the Wikipedia summary.
events.delivers: Conditional on the Alon–Tarsi conjecture for Latin squares: the vector-space version of the conjecture for even n over fields of characteristic zero. Nothing unconditional.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, unconditionally.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture. Conditional support only.

events.what_happened: M. Wild proved the conjecture for strongly base-orderable matroids. The year 1994 comes from the Open Problem Garden reference list, and the secondary sources (Wikipedia summary, search summaries) agree on the class. Paper not opened.
events.delivers: Every strongly base-orderable matroid, of every rank n, as reported in the secondary sources.
events.remains: All matroids outside the strongly base-orderable class, and so the general statement.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture. A restricted class.

events.what_happened: Wendy Chan, 'An exchange property of matroid', Discrete Mathematics 146 (1995) 299–302. The citation comes from search results and the Wikipedia summary, and the paper was not opened. Per the Wikipedia summary, Chan proved the conjecture for n = 3 across all matroid types.
events.delivers: The full statement for n = 3: all matroids of rank 3 with three disjoint bases.
events.remains: n ≥ 4 for every matroid.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (citation only; the paper was not opened)
checked_by.where: Discrete Mathematics 146 (1995) 299–302, citation via search results; no URL opened

events.doubts: Matroid Union (opened) says the conjecture 'holds for n = 3 and n = 4'. The rank-4 part of that statement rests on the unpublished Cheung manuscript, so the Matroid Union wording is not a second source for n = 3. Not a doubt about Chan's n = 3 result.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: a proof for n = 3.

events.what_happened: Drisko (1997, and a further case in 1998) and Glynn (2010) established the Alon–Tarsi conjecture for Latin squares for n = p ± 1 (p prime). Through the Huang–Rota and Onn reduction, that gives the vector-space version of the conjecture over fields of characteristic zero for those n. The papers were not opened. The years and the identity of each special case come from the Open Problem Garden reference list and search summaries, which disagree on whether Drisko's case is p+1 or p−1 (see disputes).
events.delivers: Vector spaces over fields of characteristic zero with n = p ± 1 for a prime p, and n = p in one source. Not matroids in general, and not positive characteristic.
events.remains: Every other n. General matroids. Positive characteristic.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, restricted to vector spaces over characteristic-zero fields with n = p ± 1.

events.what_happened: Timothy Chow, 'Reduction of Rota's basis conjecture to a problem on three bases', arXiv math/0504367 (v1 18 April 2005; v4 8 September 2008 with the comment 'Accepted version, SIAM J. Discrete Math.; minor errors in previous version corrected'). Chow shows that the conjecture follows from a three-basis statement: for a rank-n matroid that is a disjoint union of three bases, and disjoint independent sets I₁,…,Iₙ with |Iᵢ| ≤ 3, there is an n×3 grid holding each element once, with Iᵢ in row i, whose three columns are bases. The paper also reports that the two-basis analogue is false (search summaries cite the graphic matroid of K4 with the three pairs of non-meeting edges as rows; I did not verify this in the paper).
events.revisions: v1 18 Apr 2005; v2 18 May 2005; v3 29 Apr 2008; v4 8 Sep 2008 (accepted version, SIAM J. Discrete Math.).
events.delivers: A reduction, not a case. If the three-basis statement held for all n, Rota's conjecture would follow. It also gives the (false) two-basis analogue as a counterexample, which is a different question.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The three-basis statement that the reduction needs is reported false (see mcdiarmid-2008 and harvey-kiraly-lau-2011), so the reduction gives no route to the conjecture as written.

checked_by.who: SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics (refereed journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper; the arXiv v4 comment says 'Accepted version, SIAM J. Discrete Math.'. Volume 23(1), 2009, per search results.

events.doubts: The reduction's key statement (the three-basis version) has been reported false. Two sources give different refuters: a search summary of Chow's v4 credits Colin McDiarmid, and the Matroid Union post (opened; a 2014 comment by Jim Geelen) credits Harvey, Király and Lau. Neither is verified in the paper, and the arXiv v4 abstract page's comment does not mention either. Chow's own remark that the paper's interest is reduced is in the search summary, not read in the paper.
events.direction: Neutral on Rota's conjecture: a reduction, to a statement later reported false.
events.object: Counterexample to the two-basis analogue, not to Rota's statement: the graphic matroid of K4 with the three pairs of non-meeting edges as rows, per search summaries of the paper. Not checked in the paper.

events.what_happened: Jim Geelen and Peter Humphries, 'Rota's basis conjecture for paving matroids', SIAM J. Discrete Math. (2006). The title and year come from the TU Berlin course copy in search results and from the Wikipedia summary; the paper was not opened.
events.delivers: Every paving matroid of every rank n.
events.remains: Matroids that are not paving, and so the general statement.

checked_by.who: SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics (refereed journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (citation only; not opened)
checked_by.where: Citation via search results; no URL opened

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, for paving matroids.

events.what_happened: Geelen and Webb show that every family of n bases of a rank-n matroid has at least ⌈√(n−1)⌉ disjoint transversal bases, or equivalently that the first Ω(√n) columns of a suitable arrangement can be bases. The publication (SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2007, per the Wikipedia summary) was not opened. Dong and Geelen (2017) describe their own paper as an improvement on this bound.
events.delivers: At least ⌈√(n−1)⌉ disjoint transversal bases for every rank-n matroid. A quantity-moving partial result: the count of disjoint transversal bases is the conjecture's own quantity, but this is far below n.
events.remains: The count is short of n by a large margin, and the exact grid is not established.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture. A partial lower bound.

events.what_happened: Not about Rota's conjecture as stated: a counterexample to Chow's three-basis statement, credited to Colin McDiarmid. A search summary says a note in Chow's newest arXiv version (v4, 8 September 2008) reports it. The v4 abstract page's comment does not mention it, and the PDF body could not be read, so the claim is unverified. The date is recorded as the year 2008 (on or before 8 September 2008 if the note is in v4).
events.revisions: Claimed for arXiv math/0504367 v4 (8 Sep 2008); not confirmed in the text.
events.delivers: Refutes the three-basis statement that Chow's reduction relies on. It says nothing about Rota's conjecture itself, but it blocks this reduction route.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: Unverified in the paper. Attribution conflicts with Matroid Union, which credits Harvey, Király and Lau (see disputes).
events.direction: Against the reduction route. Neutral on Rota's conjecture.
events.object: A counterexample to the three-basis statement, found by McDiarmid. Its construction is not described in any source I read.

events.what_happened: Not about Rota's conjecture as stated: Nicholas Harvey, Tamás Király and Lap Chi Lau, 'On Disjoint Common Bases in Two Matroids' (SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2011 per Matroid Union). The SIAM page is paywalled and was not opened. They give a counterexample to a conjecture of Chow on common-base packing. Per the search summary, Chow's conjecture generalises Rota's, and Chow showed it implies Rota's for each b. A Matroid Union comment by Jim Geelen credits this paper with refuting Chow's three-basis reduction.
events.delivers: Refutes Chow's general common-base-packing conjecture, which generalises Rota's conjecture. Does not refute Rota's conjecture as stated.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.

checked_by.who: SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics (refereed journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (citation only; the SIAM page is paywalled)

events.doubts: Attribution conflicts with the McDiarmid counterexample (see disputes). The construction was not read.
events.direction: Against a generalisation of the conjecture. No direct bearing on Rota's conjecture as stated.
events.object: A counterexample to Chow's common-base-packing conjecture. Construction not read.

events.what_happened: Michael Cheung, 'Computational proof of Rota's basis conjecture for matroids of rank 4', an unpublished manuscript dated 2012 (per a reference list; the manuscript was not opened). Polymath 12 (blog post of 5 May 2017, opened) says the manuscript reports that the n = 4 case is true for all matroids, calls it 'an impressive computation', and says it 'deserves independent verification'. Luke Pebody started that verification and, as far as the post says, did not complete it.
events.delivers: If correct, the n = 4 case for all matroids, by computer search. Settles that one value of n.
events.remains: n ≥ 5 and every other rank.
events.doubts: Unpublished and computational. The Polymath 12 post (May 2017) asks for independent verification and records that a check was started but not completed. Later papers cite it as unpublished (search summaries of Bucić et al. and Pokrovskiy). The independent SAT result of Kirchweger et al. (2022) also establishes the rank-4 case, so it cross-checks the claim without verifying the manuscript.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture for n = 4.
people: Luke Pebody (started a check, did not complete it, per the Polymath post)

events.what_happened: Not about Rota's conjecture as stated: the online version. Bollen and Draisma (arXiv 1312.5953; December 2013 by identifier; the page was not opened) fix each row's permutation before the later rows are revealed. The Matroid Union post by Jan Draisma (24 February 2014, opened) says the online version is false for general matroids, that for even n a non-vanishing ELS(n) − OLS(n) gives an online algorithm, and that for odd n an online algorithm can be forced to err. Polymath 12 (opened, May 2017) reports that the achievable count lies between n/3 + c and n/2 + c for general matroids.
events.delivers: The online variant only: for general matroids the online version fails, and the achievable count is between n/3 + c and n/2 + c.
events.remains: The offline conjecture as stated, which is problem_asks.
events.direction: A changed question (online). Negative for that variant. No bearing on the offline statement.

events.what_happened: Not about Rota's basis conjecture: Geelen, Gerards and Whittle were credited in 2013 with a proof of Rota's conjecture on forbidden minors for matroids, a different conjecture with a similar name. The Open Problem Garden entry was edited on 28 August 2013 to say the basis conjecture had been proved by Geelen, Gerards and Whittle (2013). A comment on 4 October 2013 (Vadim Lioubimov) showed the announcement concerned the minor conjecture, and the status was restored to unsolved. Jon Noel replied 'My mistake' on 11 October 2013. The 2014 Kalai post on the matroid result is linked from Kalai's 2025 post and was not opened.
events.revisions: OPG status change added 28 Aug 2013; removed after comment 4 Oct 2013.
events.delivers: Concerns Rota's forbidden-minor conjecture for matroids. Nothing about the basis conjecture.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.

withdrawn.what: Open Problem Garden status statement that Rota's basis conjecture had been proved by Geelen, Gerards and Whittle (2013). It was removed after a comment on 4 October 2013 showed that the announcement concerned a different conjecture.

events.direction: None for this problem. A namesake confusion.

events.what_happened: Sally Dong and Jim Geelen, 'Improved bounds for Rota's Basis Conjecture', arXiv 1709.00075 (v1 31 August 2017; v2 5 February 2018; the comments field says 'Accepted for publication in Combinatorica'). Opened abstract: for disjoint bases B₁,…,Bₙ of a rank-n matroid there are at least ⌊n/(6⌈log n⌉)⌋ disjoint transversals that are also bases.
events.delivers: At least ⌊n/(6⌈log n⌉)⌋ disjoint transversal bases for every rank-n matroid. A quantity-moving partial result, below the later BKPS bound.
events.remains: The count is short of n by a factor of about log n. The exact grid is not established.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper, per the arXiv comments field. Publication not verified.

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture. A partial lower bound.

events.what_happened: Matija Bucić, Matthew Kwan, Alexey Pokrovskiy and Benny Sudakov, 'Halfway to Rota's basis conjecture', arXiv 1810.07462 (v1 17 October 2018; v2 3 August 2019; v3 3 April 2020). They show that one can always find (1/2 − o(1))n disjoint transversal bases, for vector spaces and for matroids, improving Ω(n/log n). IMRN 2020(21): 8007–8026, DOI 10.1093/imrn/rnaa004 (per search results; the IMRN page was not opened). The abstract was opened.
events.delivers: At least (1/2 − o(1))n disjoint transversal bases for every rank-n matroid with n bases. A quantity-moving asymptotic bound. Reaches the conjecture's count only up to a factor of about 2.
events.remains: The exact count n and the exact grid.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper, per search results (DOI 10.1093/imrn/rnaa004). Not verified on the IMRN page.
checked_by.where: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.07462 (journal reference via search; the DOI was not opened)

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture. An asymptotic bound on the count.

events.what_happened: Benjamin Friedman and Sean McGuinness, 'Girth conditions and Rota's basis conjecture', arXiv 1908.01216 (v1 3 August 2019; v2 2 September 2020; no journal listed). Opened abstract: if the matroid has girth at least n − o(√n), and no element lies in more than o(√n) of the bases, then at least n − o(n) disjoint rainbow bases exist. The abstract says it extends the paving result of Geelen and Humphries and uses the cascade idea of Bucić et al.
events.delivers: Under a girth condition of n − o(√n) and bounded multiplicity of elements across the bases, n − o(n) disjoint rainbow bases. A restricted class, under hypotheses on the matroid.
events.remains: General matroids, and the exact count n.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, under hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Alexey Pokrovskiy, 'Rota's Basis Conjecture holds asymptotically', arXiv 2008.06045 (v1 13 August 2020, the only version listed). Opened abstract: for a rank-n matroid with n bases, it is possible to find n − o(n) disjoint rainbow independent sets of size n − o(n). Journal: Proc. AMS 153 (2025), no. 10, pp. 4101–4118, DOI 10.1090/proc/16581, per search results. The AMS page returned HTTP 403 and was not read. A Waterloo talk on 25 September 2020 is in search results only.
events.revisions: v1 13 Aug 2020 (only arXiv version listed). Journal version PAMS 2025 per search results.
events.delivers: Asymptotic: n − o(n) disjoint rainbow independent sets of size n − o(n) for a rank-n matroid with n bases. A quantity-moving asymptotic result. The full text was not read.
events.remains: The exact count n, the exact size n, and the exact grid. The abstract does not state an exact case.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society (refereed journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 2025 (per search results). The AMS page was not readable.
checked_by.where: https://doi.org/10.1090/proc/16581 (returned HTTP 403 after redirect; not read)

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture. An asymptotic result on the count and the size.

events.what_happened: Sean McGuinness, 'Rota's Basis Conjecture for Matroids with Density Close to One', arXiv 2107.07024 (v1 14 July 2021; v3 30 June 2022; no journal listed). Opened abstract: a matroid on n + k elements (rank n) has n − k³ disjoint rainbow bases. The rendered abstract shows a constant 'b' that appears to be a typo, so I have recorded the form as printed in the abstract.
events.revisions: v1 14 Jul 2021; v3 30 Jun 2022 (v2 not checked).
events.delivers: Matroids with only n + k elements for small k: at least n − k³ disjoint rainbow bases. A restricted class, defined by a near-minimal ground set.
events.remains: Matroids with many more elements than their rank, and the exact count n.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, under the near-minimal ground-set hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Not about Rota's conjecture as stated: Damir Yeliussizov, 'Saturation of Rota's basis conjecture', arXiv 2107.12926 (v1 27 July 2021; no journal listed). Opened abstract: an asymptotic saturation-type version, using the connection between Tao's slice rank and unstable tensors from geometric invariant theory.
events.delivers: An asymptotic saturation-type variant. A different question from the conjecture as stated.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: A changed question (saturation). No direct bearing on the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Not about Rota's conjecture as stated (changed hypothesis: random inputs): Lisa Sauermann, 'Rota's basis conjecture holds for random bases of vector spaces', arXiv 2203.17121 (v1 31 March 2022; 17 pages; no journal listed on arXiv). Opened arXiv abstract: when the n bases are chosen uniformly at random from the bases of F_q^n, the conjecture holds with probability 1 − o(1); the same holds for bases whose vectors have entries in a fixed finite set S. A search result (NSF public-access record) lists it in the European Journal of Combinatorics, and Montgomery–Sauermann cite a 2024 Sauermann paper, which may be that journal version; neither was confirmed.
events.revisions: v1 31 Mar 2022; a journal-stage version is listed on the NSF record (date not confirmed).
events.delivers: The conjecture holds with high probability for random bases over a finite field. Restricted to random inputs, not for every family of bases.
events.remains: The deterministic statement for every family of n disjoint bases in every rank-n matroid.

checked_by.who: European Journal of Combinatorics (refereed journal), per the NSF record
checked_by.what_they_did: Published, per the NSF public-access record. Publication year not confirmed.

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, for random inputs. A different question from the one as stated.

events.what_happened: Markus Kirchweger, Manfred Scheucher and Stefan Szeider, 'A SAT Attack on Rota's Basis Conjecture', SAT 2022 (LIPIcs vol. 236, article 4; published 28 July 2022 per the Dagstuhl record). Opened Dagstuhl record: the authors extend SAT modulo Symmetries (a CDCL SAT solver plus an external lexicographic minimality checker) to matroids, and 'establish that the conjecture holds for all matroids of rank 4' and certain special cases of rank 5. The framework can also produce DRAT proofs. Preprint date not checked; the date given is the conference publication date.
events.delivers: The conjecture for every matroid of rank 4 (n = 4), and for certain special rank-5 matroids. A computer-search result that settles one value of n, and some special cases of n = 5.
events.remains: n ≥ 5 in general, and the rest of rank 5.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for peer-reviewed proceedings

events.directly_checkable: The rank-4 claim is a finite enumeration over matroids of rank 4. The paper's dataset for rank 4 is archived with the source code on Zenodo, per the paper's abstract page; I did not open it.
events.doubts: Unclear whether the rank-4 result itself is certified by the DRAT proofs the framework can output. The abstract says only that the framework 'was also extended to produce DRAT proofs'.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture. Settles n = 4 and some special cases of n = 5.
events.object: No object exhibited. The result is a universal statement over all matroids of rank 4, checked by SAT search, and it does not exhibit a counterexample or a construction.

events.what_happened: Shun-ichi Maezawa and Akiko Yazawa, 'Special Case of Rota's Basis Conjecture on Graphic Matroids', Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 29(3) (2022), article P3.63, DOI 10.37236/10835 (published 23 September 2022 per the EJC page, opened). The paper proves the graphic case where each colour class is a spanning star: the edge-coloured graph decomposes into rainbow spanning trees. Preprint date not checked, so the year is recorded.
events.delivers: Graphic matroids of connected multigraphs with n vertices (rank n − 1) whose n − 1 colour classes are spanning stars. A restricted class.
events.remains: Colour classes that are not stars, and all non-graphic matroids.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, for graphic matroids with star colour classes.

events.what_happened: Anant Asthana and Shreev Goyal, 'Rainbow Stars and Rota's Basis Conjecture for Graphic Matroids', arXiv 2310.19242 (v1 30 October 2023; v2 1 November 2023; no journal listed). Opened abstract: extends the star case to stars with all distinct centres, all the same centre, or one of two centres; characterises when a monochromatic star decomposition can be made rainbow; and shows the analogous statement fails when stars are replaced by paths.
events.delivers: Subcases of the graphic star case. A counterexample to the path analogue, which is a different question. A restricted class.
events.remains: The general graphic case and all other matroids.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture on the star subcases. The path analogue fails, which concerns a different question.
events.object: A graph with colour classes that are paths, for which the rainbow-decomposition statement fails. Construction not read.

events.what_happened: Richard Montgomery and Lisa Sauermann, 'Asymptotically-tight packing and covering with transversal bases in Rota's basis conjecture', arXiv 2508.05601 (v1 only, submitted 7 August 2025; 33 pages; math.CO; no journal reference on the arXiv page). Theorem 1.5 (asymptotic packing): for any ε > 0 and n sufficiently large in terms of ε, any n bases of a rank-n matroid have at least (1−ε)n disjoint transversal bases. Theorem 1.6 (asymptotic covering): the union of the n bases can be covered by at most (1+ε)n transversal bases. The packing bound improves BKPS (1/2 − o(1))n. The covering bound improves Aharoni–Berger's 2n and the Polymath 12 bound 2n − 2. The authors write that Conjecture 1.1 'remains widely open, even for the case of vector spaces'. The paper states no theorem for any fixed n and no exact count. Funding: ERC grant 947978 (Montgomery) and DFG Heisenberg (Sauermann), per the footnotes.
events.revisions: v1 only (7 Aug 2025) as of the arXiv abstract page. No later version found.
events.delivers: Asymptotic packing: (1−o(1))n disjoint transversal bases for every rank-n matroid, for n large. Asymptotic covering: the union covered by (1+o(1))n transversal bases. These move the conjecture's own count (n disjoint transversal bases) to (1−o(1))n for large n. They establish neither the exact count n nor the grid for any n, and they do not reach the sizes the conjecture asks for.
events.remains: The exact existence of n disjoint transversal bases for each n (and so the grid); every n below the 'sufficiently large' threshold; exact covering with n transversal bases.

checked_by.qualification: Research combinatorialist writing a blog post. Commentary, not a verification. His current position was not checked here.
checked_by.what_they_did: Blog post of 9 September 2025 calling the result 'a major breakthrough on the beautiful Rota's basis conjecture' and summarising the bound. No check of the argument is described.

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture: the count of disjoint transversal bases approaches the conjectured n asymptotically. No counterexample, and no case of the exact statement.

events.what_happened: Stephen Arndt, Benjamin Moseley, Kirk Pruhs, Chaitanya Swamy and Michael Zlatin, 'Approximation Algorithms for Matroid-Intersection Coloring with Applications to Rota's Basis Conjecture', arXiv 2604.03735 (cs.DS; v1 only, 4 April 2026). Opened abstract page: for k matroids on a common ground set, polynomial-time algorithms partition the elements into the fewest independent colour classes, with an approximation ratio depending only on k. The paper says it gives 'the first polynomial-time constructive algorithm for an asymptotic variant of Rota's Basis Conjecture', constructivising Montgomery and Sauermann's asymptotic result. It does not prove Rota's Basis Conjecture or any instance of it.
events.delivers: An algorithmic version of the asymptotic result of Montgomery and Sauermann, for matroid-intersection colouring. Explicitly not a proof of any instance of the conjecture.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Asymptotic and algorithmic. Cuts toward the conjecture only in the asymptotic sense of Montgomery–Sauermann.

events.what_happened: Gergely Bérczi (Aarhus University, per search results), 'Evolving Local Corrections for Global Constructions in Combinatorics', arXiv 2603.06692 (v1 only, submitted 4 March 2026; 52 pages including appendix; math.GM; no journal reference). The paper states its three case studies were 'carried out using AlphaEvolve as an experimental engine for proposing and iteratively refining such certificates'. Its Rota's Basis Conjecture section (Section 5) studies linear matroids over F₂ of rank 5 (Experiment A), rank 7 (Experiment B) and ranks 5 to 13 (Experiment C). It evolves a scoring policy for a greedy local-exchange engine that picks the highest-scoring insert or repair move. Reported runs: Experiment A, 12-vector pool, 200 instances, success rate 1.00; Experiment B, pool about 16, 100 instances, success rate 1.00; Experiment C, pool ⌈2.2n⌉, 60 instances, one rollout, overall success rate 1.00. The author states: 'The goal is not to resolve the conjecture' (Section 1.3). The Rota statements are the author's own Conjectures 9 and 10 (rank-5 and rank-7 toy cases for circuit-rich pools) and Conjecture 11 (n in {5,7,9,11,13}; success within O(n²) steps). The paper claims no theorem about the conjecture and no new bound on the count of disjoint transversal bases.
events.revisions: v1 only (4 Mar 2026) as of the arXiv abstract page and HTML.
events.delivers: Computational success on sampled F₂-linear matroids of rank 5 to 13, by an evolved policy. Each reported run is a set of disjoint transversal bases for the sampled instances. No theorem, and no bound for general matroids or for the conjecture's general statement.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The result is limited to F₂-linear matroids of small rank and to sampled instances.
events.directly_checkable: Each reported instance's output is a grid of bases that can be checked by linear algebra over F₂. The paper's own verifier was used for the runs. I did not check any output independently.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: no counterexample among the sampled toy instances. Not a proof or a disproof.
events.object: An evolved scoring policy: a greedy local-exchange rule that, on sampled F₂-linear matroids of rank 5 to 13 built from random or structured vector pools, produced rainbow transversal bases (a grid of bases) with success rate 1.00 on the reported runs. The object is an explicit algorithm for those instances, and each output is a certificate checkable by linear algebra over F₂. It is not a construction for general matroids.

systems.name: AlphaEvolve
systems.what_it_did: The evolutionary search engine that evolved the scoring policy for the Rota experiments in Section 5 (Experiments A to C). The policies are what the paper reports as succeeding on the sampled F₂ instances. The paper calls AlphaEvolve 'a construction-driven search engine' (Section 1) and says that the experiments were carried out with it. It is a Google DeepMind system, per the acknowledgement 'the Google DeepMind AlphaEvolve team'.
systems.basis_quote: The experiments in this paper were carried out by using the evolutionary search model AlphaEvolve

events.what_happened: Not about Rota's basis conjecture: Alexander Divoux, Chayim Lowen and Shouda Wang, 'Matroid flat counts are not unimodal', arXiv 2607.22515 (v1 only, 24 July 2026; 8 pages; math.CO). disputes.summary: Who refuted Chow's three-basis reduction is unresolved. A search summary of Chow's v4 credits Colin McDiarmid with a counterexample to the three-basis statement. The Matroid Union post (opened; comment by Jim Geelen) says it was refuted by Harvey, Király and Lau (2011). Harvey et al. refute a general common-base-packing conjecture of Chow's, which Chow said generalises Rota's. The v4 abstract page's comment does not mention either refuter, and the PDF was unreadable.

In 2013 the Open Problem Garden briefly recorded Rota's basis conjecture as proved by Geelen, Gerards and Whittle. The announced result concerned Rota's forbidden-minor conjecture for matroids. The status was restored to unsolved on 4 October 2013 after a comment. Recorded here for audit only; no current dispute about the basis conjecture.

Rank-4 status. Matroid Union (opened) says the conjecture 'holds for n = 3 and n = 4'. The n = 4 part rests on Cheung's unpublished 2012 manuscript, which later papers cite as unpublished. Kirchweger, Scheucher and Szeider (SAT 2022, opened) establish all matroids of rank 4 by SAT, peer-reviewed. The Wikipedia summary lists only n ≤ 3 as proved for all matroids. The rank-4 case is therefore supported by a refereed computer proof, but its independence from the Cheung claim is not verified.
Dong–Geelen bound: the arXiv abstract (opened) gives ⌊n/(6⌈log n⌉)⌋. Several search summaries give n/(7 log n). I record the abstract's form.

Drisko and Glynn cases: search summaries attribute p+1 and p−1 to different authors (one source reverses them), and a Kumar–Landsberg search summary says the Alon–Tarsi Latin-square conjecture is known up to n = 24, while another summary says n ≤ 8. This affects only the conditional route through Alon–Tarsi for characteristic zero, not the n = p ± 1 results themselves, which are cited independently.

summary: The conjecture is open in every source I could open. I found no claimed resolution, no counterexample and no AI-produced proof. Its own quantity, the number of disjoint transversal bases, has moved only asymptotically: BKPS (2018) gave (1/2 − o(1))n, and Montgomery and Sauermann (arXiv 2508.05601, 7 August 2025, v1 only, no journal reference) prove (1−ε)n disjoint transversal bases and (1+ε)n covering transversal bases for n large in terms of ε (Theorems 1.5 and 1.6). Their own text says Conjecture 1.1 'remains widely open, even for the case of vector spaces'. Kalai's September 2025 post calls it a 'major breakthrough', which is commentary and not a check. Whether that movement counts is close: the count moved is the conjecture's own quantity, but only asymptotically and for large n, so the exact statement for each n is untouched. Arndt, Moseley, Pruhs, Swamy and Zlatin (arXiv 2604.03735, 4 April 2026) make the asymptotic variant constructive and say they prove no instance. Bérczi (arXiv 2603.06692, 4 March 2026) runs AlphaEvolve on F₂-linear toy matroids of rank 5 to 13. The paper's Rota section evolves policies that succeed on the sampled instances, with success rate 1.00 on the reported runs, and states the author's own Conjectures 9 to 11 about those toy cases. The author writes 'The goal is not to resolve the conjecture'. This is the only in-window event I found with AI involvement that touches the problem. AlphaEvolve is entered in ai.systems on the paper's own sentence that the experiments were carried out with it. Whether its output is load-bearing is for the later pass: it produces computational certificates for specific small instances, not a theorem. The Gemini models named in the paper's AI declaration ('gemini-2.5-pro and gemini-3-pro models to generate summaries') generate experiment summaries, not mathematics, so they are not in ai.systems. The declaration also mentions unnamed 'code generation outside the AlphaEvolve system for vibe-coding evaluation harnesses'. Pre-window history is recorded as events. Chan (1995) proved n = 3. Geelen and Humphries (2006) proved paving matroids. Drisko and Glynn (1997 to 2010) proved the characteristic-zero vector-space case for n = p ± 1, conditional on nothing for those n. Cheung (2012) claimed n = 4 by computer, unpublished. Kirchweger, Scheucher and Szeider (SAT 2022, refereed) establish all matroids of rank 4 by SAT, which is not AI. Pokrovskiy (arXiv 2020, PAMS 2025 per search) proved an asymptotic rainbow-set result. Chow's 2005 reduction to a three-basis statement no longer gives a route, since that statement is reported false, with the refuter disputed. Discounted events are recorded as such: the 2013 Geelen–Gerards–Whittle namesake claim (withdrawn on the OPG page), the Bollen–Draisma online variant, Yeliussizov's saturation variant, Sauermann's random-bases variant, Asthana–Goyal's graphic-star subcases with a path counterexample, and Divoux–Lowen–Wang 2026 on Rota's unimodality conjecture, which the Breakthrough Tracker says a ChatGPT 5.6 Pro suggestion contributed to but which is not in the authors' abstract page. Two source-quality caveats: the Wikipedia article and the Bérczi and Montgomery–Sauermann texts were read through a summarising fetch tool, so their quotations should be checked against the source. The Wikipedia summary lists nothing after 2009 and does not mention Montgomery–Sauermann.
competing_reading: Read as a count-moving result, Montgomery–Sauermann moves the conjecture's own quantity, the number of disjoint transversal bases, from n/2 to (1−o(1))n, so it is a substantial bound on the conjecture's main quantity, and a later pass could count it as progress on that quantity. Read as a statement about the problem, the problem asks for exactly n disjoint transversal bases for every n, and the 2025 result gives this only up to a factor 1 ± o(1) for n large, with no exact case. On the Bérczi experiment, one reading is that AlphaEvolve produced explicit certificates for sampled instances of the problem's grid, which is a constructive instance of the statement. The other is that the paper frames these as toy experiments, with no theorem and no claim about the conjecture, and that the instances are restricted to F₂-linear matroids of rank at most 13.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The rest of the Montgomery–Sauermann text, past the middle of Section 7 and including the references. This would confirm there is no exact-n corollary and no AI statement, and that Theorems 1.5 and 1.6 carry no extra restriction. (b) The PDF of Bérczi (arXiv 2603.06692) read directly, to confirm the AlphaEvolve sentences and the AI declaration verbatim, and the Section 5 wording of Conjectures 9 to 11. (c) Whether Montgomery–Sauermann or Bérczi has a journal version or a published referee report. (d) Cheung's 2012 manuscript or an independent computer verification of n = 4 beyond the SAT result. (e) The Harvey–Király–Lau paper and the Chow v4 PDF, to settle who refuted the three-basis statement. (f) An arXiv math.CO search for 'Rota basis' and 'transversal bases' sorted by date, since my search tool may not index the most recent preprints.

event.what_happened: Richard Montgomery and Lisa Sauermann, 'Asymptotically-tight packing and covering with transversal bases in Rota's basis conjecture', arXiv 2508.05601 (v1 only, submitted 7 August 2025; 33 pages; math.CO; no journal reference on the arXiv page). Theorem 1.5 (asymptotic packing): for any ε > 0 and n sufficiently large in terms of ε, any n bases of a rank-n matroid have at least (1−ε)n disjoint transversal bases. Theorem 1.6 (asymptotic covering): the union of the n bases can be covered by at most (1+ε)n transversal bases. The packing bound improves BKPS (1/2 − o(1))n. The covering bound improves Aharoni–Berger's 2n and the Polymath 12 bound 2n − 2. The authors write that Conjecture 1.1 'remains widely open, even for the case of vector spaces'. The paper states no theorem for any fixed n and no exact count. Funding: ERC grant 947978 (Montgomery) and DFG Heisenberg (Sauermann), per the footnotes.
event.revisions: v1 only (7 Aug 2025) as of the arXiv abstract page. No later version found.
event.delivers: Asymptotic packing: (1−o(1))n disjoint transversal bases for every rank-n matroid, for n large. Asymptotic covering: the union covered by (1+o(1))n transversal bases. These move the conjecture's own count (n disjoint transversal bases) to (1−o(1))n for large n. They establish neither the exact count n nor the grid for any n, and they do not reach the sizes the conjecture asks for.
event.remains: The exact existence of n disjoint transversal bases for each n (and so the grid); every n below the 'sufficiently large' threshold; exact covering with n transversal bases.

judgement.why: The only post-snapshot event that moves the problem is Montgomery–Sauermann. It improves the conjecture's own count of disjoint transversal bases to (1−o(1))n for large n, which is a bound and not an exact case, and only Kalai's commentary engages with it, so it stays unreviewed. Arndt et al. make a known asymptotic result constructive and prove no instance of the conjecture: none. Bérczi's AlphaEvolve runs certify sampled F₂-linear instances, which is a finite check: instances. Its AI role is generated, because the evolved policy produced the certificates, but the instances scope discards the event anyway. Divoux–Lowen–Wang is about a different Rota conjecture, a namesake: variant. Before the snapshot, the restricted classes and fixed ranks (n=3, n=4, paving, strongly base-orderable, graphic stars, char-0 vector spaces with n=p±1) are cases, and none is whole. Friedman–McGuinness and McGuinness 2021 give n−o(n) or n−k³ counts under hypotheses; I scored them as bound rather than case because they move the count without settling the exact statement.
judgement.doubts: Drisko–Glynn was scored as an unconditional case, which assumes Alon–Tarsi is proved for those n, as the record states. The Divoux event's tracker-reported ChatGPT credit does not appear in the authors' text and is not in ai.systems. In any case the event is a variant.
